# Deploy platform-managed vector store via the Platform Operator

## Description

Deliver the platform-managed vector store posture: administrators can deploy
a managed vector database (Milvus) through the Platform Operator with
productized images and a supported lifecycle. This epic executes only if the
posture decision selects the platform-managed path; if the
external-connection-only posture is chosen instead, this work is removed.

## Scope

- Operator support for deploying the managed vector database as part of the
  platform, with productized/container images and supported lifecycle
  (install, upgrade, scale) owned by the platform rather than the customer.
- Deployment surface suitable for regulated customers who need a
  platform-managed vector database with supported images and lifecycle.
- The connection mechanism and resources through which other platform
  components (Llama Stack distributions, Dashboard) discover and attach to
  the deployed managed vector store — the artifact downstream work builds
  against.
- Disconnected-environment support considerations identified in the posture
  evaluation (productized images usable without external dependencies).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an administrator installs the platform with the managed posture
  selected, when they deploy the managed vector store through the Platform
  Operator, then the deployment completes using productized images without
  manual manifest editing.
- Given a deployed managed vector store, when a platform component or
  administrator needs to discover its connection details, then a
  well-defined connection mechanism/resources exist that the Llama Stack and
  Dashboard integrations can build against.
- Given the managed vector store is part of the supported platform, then its
  lifecycle (upgrades, scaling) is handled through the Platform Operator's
  supported mechanisms, not ad-hoc scripts.
- The rollback story for the managed deployment is documented and validated
  (deploy can be undone / reconfigured without data-plane surgery).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0), managed-path disjunct: administrators can deploy the managed
  vector store through the Platform Operator with productized images.

# Consume managed vector store as Llama Stack RAG provider

## Description

Enable Llama Stack distributions to consume the platform-managed vector
store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs. Executes
only under the platform-managed posture, building on the connection
mechanism the operator deployment provides.

## Scope

- Wire the managed vector store into Llama Stack's RAG provider plugin
  surface (Llama Stack already lists Milvus/vector providers as an optional
  RAG dependency in its architecture context) so distributions use it
  automatically once deployed.
- Configuration flow from the operator-deployed managed vector store's
  connection resources into Llama Stack distribution configuration — no
  hand-editing of distribution configs.
- Validation that a Llama Stack distribution can serve RAG workloads
  (embedding storage and retrieval) against the managed vector store.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a platform-managed vector store deployed through the Platform
  Operator, when a Llama Stack distribution is created, then the
  distribution uses the managed vector store as its RAG provider without
  hand-editing the distribution config.
- Given a distribution wired to the managed vector store, when a RAG
  workload stores and retrieves embeddings, then the operations succeed
  against the managed vector store.
- No manual config editing is required at any point from deployment to a
  working RAG-enabled distribution.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1), managed path: Llama Stack distributions can consume the chosen
  vector store as a RAG provider without hand-editing distribution configs.

# External vector store connection registration, validation, and management UI

## Description

Deliver the external-connection-only posture: data scientists can register an
external vector store connection (e.g. a cloud-managed vector DB they
already run) per project with validated connectivity, and manage those
connections through the Dashboard. Executes only if the posture decision
selects the external path; if the platform-managed posture is chosen, this
work is removed.

## Scope

- Per-project registration of an external vector store connection with
  validated connectivity (connection parameters validated at registration
  time; registration fails clearly when the external store is unreachable or
  credentials are wrong).
- Connection management UI in the Dashboard: registration/edit forms,
  connection lists per project, and connectivity status views, following the
  Dashboard's established per-component integration pattern.
- The connection resource format and validation contract that downstream
  consumers (Llama Stack distributions) build against.
- A sanctioned, supported way for cloud-native customers to connect stores
  they already run — no platform-managed vector database is deployed or
  supported in this posture.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a data scientist has access to an external vector store, when they
  register the connection in a project, then the platform validates
  connectivity before accepting the registration and reports failures
  clearly.
- Given a registered connection, when the data scientist views the project
  in the Dashboard, then the connection (and its validation status) is
  visible and editable through the connection management UI.
- Given a validated connection, when a downstream consumer needs the
  connection details, then a well-defined per-project connection resource
  exists that the Llama Stack integration can build against.
- Given a failed or revoked external store, when connectivity is re-checked,
  then the connection status reflects the failure without breaking the rest
  of the project.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0), external-path disjunct: data scientists can register an
  external vector store connection per project with validated connectivity.
- HLR-4 (P1), external path: the Dashboard exposes connection management UI
  for the external path.

# Posture decision: first supported vector store posture (managed vs external)

## Description

Produce the documented evaluation and decision on which vector store posture
the platform productizes first for RAG workloads: a platform-managed vector
database (operator-deployed Milvus with productized images and lifecycle) or
an external-connection-only posture (data scientists register their own
managed vector store per project). The decision is the answer to the
strategy's sole open question and determines the entire downstream
implementation structure.

## Scope

- Evaluate both postures against the strategy's stated criteria:
  supportability cost, disconnected-environment viability, and
  time-to-market.
- Weigh input from the two customer camps described in the strategy:
  regulated customers (want platform-managed, supported images, lifecycle)
  and cloud-native customers (already run managed external services, want a
  sanctioned connection path).
- Consider the platform context: Llama Stack's optional Milvus/vector
  provider dependency for RAG workflows (per Llama Stack architecture
  context), Platform Operator deployment patterns, and Dashboard
  integration cost for each posture.
- Produce a documented evaluation and a single decision: platform-managed
  (operator-deployed Milvus) or external-connection-only.
- Define what each outcome implies for downstream work (which epics execute
  under each posture), so the selected branch can start immediately.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the supportability-cost, disconnected-environment, and
  time-to-market criteria, when the evaluation is complete, then the
  trade-offs of each posture are documented against all three criteria.
- Given the documented evaluation, when the decision is recorded, then
  exactly one posture is selected as the first supported vector store
  posture, with rationale referencing the evaluation.
- Given the selected posture, when the decision is published, then the
  downstream implementation plan corresponding to that posture is identified
  (the branch epics attached to this investigation), so implementation can
  begin without further discovery.
- Shipping both postures in the same release is explicitly rejected as out
  of scope (per the strategy).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): a decision is reached, with a documented evaluation, on the
  first supported vector store posture — this epic is the entirety of HLR-1.
